Shape.Name: Sheet.3
Shape.Text:
Ghosting artifacts due to respiratory motion in head images is often seen on sedated patients, who have a deep regular cycle in their breathing pattern. This is sometimes difficult to detect as a motion problem. In this example, note how the ghosts are well defined, suggesting that the disturbance had a regular frequency (cyclical).
The source of a cyclical disturbance can be anything that has a regular, repeating rhythm (i.e. coldhead, fans, air handlers, rotating machinery, and in some cases people with deep regular breathing)

Shape.Name: Sheet.4
Shape.Text:
In this image, which has light but well defined ghosts, it appears that this sedated patient’s respiratory cycle changed at least once during the scan (Multiple, distinct ghosts).
However, notice that the small phantom in the lower right quadrant (actually a vitamin E capsule) is completely free of any ghosting.
If the cyclical interference had been anything other than the patient (i.e. RF, gradient, coldhead or external vibration) then the small phantom would also be ghosted.

Shape.Name: Sheet.5
Shape.Text: These SPT plots demonstrate the classic signature for a single axis gradient failure. A single axis gradient subsystem failure is characterized by different test parameters failing depending on the logical gradient function that the failing axis is performing. When the failing axis is performing the readout (frequency encode) function time domain echo shift is effected. When the failing axis is performing the slice select function the constant phase offset is effected. Since off center slices are most effected the constant phase offset is high on the two off center plots while the isocenter plot shows little or no constant phase failure. Often the phase plots will show a polarity shift between the two off center slices (not obvious in this example). In this example the Y axis shows greater (marginal) instability in time domain echo shift during the slice X Readout Y (Sagital) body fse test. The echo shift failure is relatively constant in all three slices (only one shown). During the slice Y readout Z test constant phase is failing severely on the offset slices at P78 and A78 while the isocenter slice is passing

Shape.Name: Sheet.6
Shape.Text: Classic signature of a single axis gradient subsystem failure in SPT

Shape.Name: Sheet.7
Shape.Text: SPT plot of Slice X Readout Y demonstrates echo center shift failures

Shape.Name: Sheet.8
Shape.Text: SPT plots for Slice Y readout Z demonstrate constant phase offset failures on the two off center slices while the isocenter plot looks normal

Shape.Name: Sheet.12
Shape.Text: Note that the instability propagates, and predominantly effects Phase and Magnitude. The fgre plots show no evidence of instability. This problem was caused by a bad tuning capacitor.

Shape.Name: Procedure.41
Shape.Text: All stability subsets are analyzed 3 ways: Echo Center Stability: Where in the A/D window the echo occurs in time and the phase change from view to view Constant Phase Stability: what the phase of the echo is after the echo center shift is removed Magnitude stability: the amplitude of the received echo
